Bethesda announces "Bethnet", company-owned mod database for Fallout 4

Personal Take: I see two problems stemming from this:

  1. Bethesda directly puts itself up as a competitor to sites like Nexus and might use its property over the IP to drive them to the ground so it gets more users on its own database. If that happens, things could get especially nastier for many of the games more lewd mods.

  2. Paid mods. I mean, come on, you know it's going to happen.

Of course it's going to happen. And unfortunately there is a huge portion of the gaming community that can't wait for that to happen. Just look at how much money Rockstar made from Shark Cards alone. There is a ridiculous amount of money to be made from more DLC/Paid Mods/Cosmetics, Bethesda is simply trying to get in on that pie. Conspiracy time: I think it's the new generation of gamers that are leading this though. Younger gamers tend to be the one obsessed with image and thus buying into these cosmetics. Also they've grown up in an era WITHOUT expansion packs where cut content for paid DLCs is the norm. Just look at the insane amount of gambling going on in the CS:GO scene, a lot of these being children that watch and are influenced by streamers and then pour money into the CS:GO economy trying to get that dragonlore.

Paid mods? Gonna happen. Fuck that.

Restricting which mods are available? Fuck that too.

This is the thin end of the wedge. The next lot of Bethesda games will have official modding tools only and sharing mods third party (ala Nexus) will be considered copyright infringement or some shit. Mark my words.

Allowing mods to run on consoles? HAHAHAHAHAHA, those shitboxes are gonna tank fucking hard. They can barely run the game vanilla.

Create a Bethesda.net account...

Go fuck yourself, Todd. I already have a perfectly fine steam account. It's bad enough that I have to login to that to use my legal license for your game, while unlicensed copies run perfectly fine without. I am not going to add to the nonsense, by logging in just so that I am allowed to login to your shitty "service".

I agree 100% I look over things on steam and if I see 3rd party authentication listed I immediately move that to unless this is exactly the type of game I love and it has great response from the community plus the lets plays look good not touching it, even then not likely for more then $20.
Why not just allow everyone to use the already existing mod database? Oh right, money.
I smell a revolt on the horizon if they try to control the modding community.
Again your forgot again. Search for "skyrim mods forever free" those guys will likely just stop modding before going to a service like this.
Did they learn nothing from the skyrim mod debacle? Fallout 4 was going to be the first game I got with my new graphics card in the summer...now I'm gonna wait and see.

I can see multiple sides of the arguement. I use nexus because its a program I've used for a long time now and its very easy. Also, "taboo" mods are only available there, steam and bethnet definitely will censor available mods.

Steam workshop is really simple for those unwilling to learn/use nexus mods but has serious drawbacks with its mod size limitations. If steam workshop support ever comes out (unlikely with bethesdas in-house approach) it will struggle.

Bethesda's approach might be beneficial however. There really isn't a more effective way to give console owners modding capabilities than this. They can't very well export nexus mods to consoles, the amount of effort that would take is unrealistic in my opinion. However the possibility is always threatening on the horizon of paid mods which a lot of us fear and sadly some modmakers really want. Some, not all.

As long as Bethesda leaves mods free, or perhaps just adds an optional donate to mod feature to their catalog, I see this as a very big boon to gamers who own Fallout 4. Consoles can mod a AAA game easily for the first time since ever. Nexus mods will still likely be the go to for PC gamers but I predict mod makers to reupload to the Bethesda catalog for consoles. Basically 2 hosts, one for PC (nexus) and one for consoles (Bethnet).

Or nexus sadly becomes host to only the taboo mods since modmakers all move to bethnet. But that might not be to bad as long as mods are free, since the end user is hardly affected.

BUT thats ONLY if bethesda leaves mods free. Otherwise I see the bethesda catalog failing, modmakers and the community getting pissed off again (valve laughing because this time they are uninvolved) and computers once again the only platform with any real mod support.

I would like to know if the in-house catalog has file size limitations though. If it does it's doomed.
